Special treatment? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I pay my taxes, I wait in line at the DMV just like everybody else. I don't expect anyone to roll out the red carpet just because I own a few trucks.

My grandkids love that place. They bounce around for hours until their faces are beet red. Then we always go get ice cream after. Pistachio, that's my favorite. Hard to find a good pistachio ice cream these days, though. A lot of places just use that artificial flavoring, you can always tell.

Better than others? Nah, not at all. I mean, we all put our pants on one leg at a time, right? Success just means I had some luck and put in the hours.

Fundamentally different? Nah. I mean, I bleed red just like anybody else. I don't think building a business changes your DNA or anything. 

I started out sweeping the warehouse floors, you know. Down at the old distribution center on 4th Street. That place was so incredibly dusty, you'd blow your nose at the end of the shift and it would just be pitch black. We used these giant industrial push brooms, the ones with the really stiff green bristles. Those bristles were made of some kind of cheap plastic, and they would actually melt if you left the broom too close to the space heaters. We had to use these massive orange kerosene heaters in the winter because the insulation in that tin building was an absolute joke. 

My buddy Frank, he used to stand so close to those heaters trying to warm up his hands that he actually singed the back of his coveralls one morning. Smelled like burnt hair and diesel fuel for a solid week in the breakroom. Frank didn't even care, though. He was a funny guy. It's all those plastic zip bags or Tupperware now. My wife bought a whole 50-piece Tupperware set off an infomercial a few years back, and half the lids have already gone missing. I swear the dishwasher eats them, just like socks in the dryer.
